content.text:
I've written the four files: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `js/engine.js` and `js/app.js`. **None of it has been run.** Running Node needed your approval and the request was declined, so I couldn't run my quick engine test or open the page in a browser. I removed the test file, so nothing else is in the folder.

- **Engine:** formula cells are parsed once and the results are cached. After any change, every value is worked out again the next time one is read, so cells that depend on the changed cell always come out current.
- **Cycles:** found by looking at which cells each formula refers to. Every cell in a loop, and every cell that depends on one, shows `#CYCLE!`, and they go back to normal values once the loop is broken. One side effect is that a reference inside an `IF` branch that isn't taken still counts toward a loop.
- **Copying formulas:** a reference that moves outside A1:J30 is written into the copied formula as `#REF!`, so that cell shows `#REF!`.
- **Things I had to decide myself:**
  - When an operation has an error on both sides, the left one wins. An error in an operand also takes priority over text used in arithmetic, so `="a"+1/0` gives `#DIV/0!`.
  - `TRUE` and `FALSE` act as 1 and 0 in comparisons too, so `=TRUE=1` is TRUE.
  - A formula that points at an empty cell, like `=A1`, gives 0.
- **Additions beyond the spec:**
  - `createSheet()` also accepts an optional starting set of cells, which the page uses to restore saved cells after a reload without creating undo steps.
  - The sheet object has an extra `all()` method that returns the raw text of every cell, which the page uses to save to localStorage.

  Calling `createSheet()` with no argument works as specified.

To check it, serve the folder with any static server and open `index.html`.
